messages:

Subject: Renewal conversation — burst capacity question

Hi Karthik,

Hope you’re well — we’re kicking off our renewal planning for Q3 and had a couple of technical questions before we loop procurement in. Our usage has been spikier recently (end-of-month reporting runs) and we want to avoid outages.

Specifically: during peaks, can requests spill over into on-demand capacity beyond our reserved GPU pools? If so, what are the latency guarantees and cost delta? Alternatively, can we set a hard cap so we never exceed the reserved pool?

Also, we’re evaluating adding 8 additional GPUs to our reserved pool at renewal — can you share an updated quote and any SLA language around throughput guarantees for the expanded pool?

Thanks — would prefer a quick call next week if that helps.

Best,
Samantha Chen
Director, ML Platform
ACME Data
[samantha.chen@acmedata.com]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Chen <samantha.chen@acmedata.com>
Cc: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acmedata.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — burst capacity question

Samantha — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers below; I’ll follow up with a concrete proposal and SLA language. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call next Tue/Wed.

1) Overflow / spillover: We support configurable spillover during peak windows. Default mode is on-demand spillover to our hosted capacity when reserved pools are saturated. That provides continued request acceptance but at a higher per-token unit cost and without the same latency SLO as reserved capacity.

2) Hard cap option: We can absolutely set a hard cap that rejects or queues excess requests once the reserved pool is full. This is common for customers who need predictable spend or strict performance boundaries.

3) Throughput guarantees: For expanded reserved pools we can add throughput targets in the addendum (e.g., X tokens/sec per GPU averaged over 1-minute P95) and include credits for sustained SLA violations. Exact numbers depend on GPU type and model profile — I’ll include recommended targets for your fleet.

I’ll send a draft quote and an SLA/burst-policy doc by Fri. Do you have a preferred time for a call? I can do Tue 6/16 11am PT or Wed 6/17 2pm PT.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Karthik / Laura — reviewed. A few concrete suggestions:

1) Pricing: For +8 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (12-month term) propose: base commit price $XX,XXX/mo; burst on-demand at 2.5x per-token rate above reserved unit. If they opt for a hard cap, offer a 10% discount on committed price to reflect reduced operational risk.

2) SLA & credits: Recommend P95 latency guarantee for reserved capacity (e.g., <120ms for short synth tokens on their model family), with a credits schedule: 5% credit for single-month breach; 15% for multi-week breach. Limit total credits per term.

3) Policy wording: Draft two short policy paragraphs for the addendum:
   - "Overflow Mode (default):" Spillover to on-demand capacity is allowed; Redwood will route traffic to on-demand pools in busy windows. On-demand requests are billed at the overage rate and are not covered by reserved latency SLOs.
   - "Hard Cap Mode (opt-in):" Customer may opt to cap usage at the reserved pool. Requests exceeding cap will be rejected with 429/queued responses. In Hard Cap Mode, overage billing does not apply; pricing for reserved commit includes a 10% discount.

I’ll edit the SLA draft and the price sheet. Karthik — please confirm what model families (name/version) ACME is running so we can lock recommended throughput numbers.

— Priyom

Samantha / Jordan — thanks for the patience. Attached is our proposal (redwood_proposal_ACME_renewal_v2.pdf) and a short SLA/burst-policy draft (sla-burst-policy-draft.docx). Highlights below so you can share with procurement: 

- Reserved expansion: +8 A100-equivalent GPUs, 12-month commitment. Quoted discount applied to commit line. (See PDF pages 2–3 for pricing.)
- Overflow handling (choose one):
  • Overflow Mode (recommended): automatic spillover to on-demand capacity when reserved pool is saturated. Overage billed at 2.5x reserved unit-rate. On-demand requests do not carry reserved latency SLOs; best-effort latency will be provided.
  • Hard Cap Mode (optional): traffic exceeding reserved pool will receive 429; no overage billing. If selected, apply a 10% lower commit price.
- SLA: P95 latency objective for traffic served from reserved pool (target <120ms for their model family). Credits defined in section 4 of the SLA draft.
- Implementation: Redwood will pre-warm wiring for the expanded pool and run a coordinated rollout during the renewal window. We’ll provide a test window to validate throughput.

Next steps: please confirm which overflow option ACME prefers and whether legal should review the attached SLA draft. If you’d like, I can schedule a short call with Priyom and our legal ops to finalize terms — propose Tue 6/23 10am PT.
